Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps: 

What I heard:
- Atlas Payments needs private connectivity for production traffic (PCI-adjacent workloads).
- Primary asks: support for Private VPC (PrivateLink or VPC peering), fine-grained IP allowlists, and short RTO for network-related incidents.
- Potential preference for a managed option (PrivateLink) to avoid cross-account route table changes, but your infra team wants pros/cons.

Options we discussed:
1) PrivateLink (our managed endpoint) — minimal route changes, we provide service endpoint and you allow the interface endpoints. Requires AWS account IDs, region, and the subnets for interface endpoints.
2) VPC Peering — bidirectional routing; requires CIDR non-overlap and route table updates on both sides. Good for low-latency internal traffic but needs more infra coordination.
3) IP allowlist (host-level or NAT) — for customers that prefer egress via a static NAT; we can provide a set of egress IPs for allowlisting or support a partner NAT setup.

Attachments: I attached our "redwood-private-vpc-networking-guide.pdf" that includes diagrams and a checklist (what we need from your team).

Proposed next steps:
- You: share preferred option (PrivateLink vs Peering) and who on your network team will own the deep-dive.
- You: provide AWS account IDs and region(s) you want to connect (if PrivateLink).
- Redwood: schedule a 60-minute deep-dive (networking + security) with our infra engineer (Dev) and delivery lead (Sean).
- I'll also surface what changes (if any) would look like for Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC in case you want to avoid the networking work.

Proposed slots: Mon 2/22 10-12 PT, Tue 2/23 1-3 PT - or send a calendar link and we'll align.

Thanks - looking forward to locking this in.

--Marissa

Hi Alex / Raj -

Short answers:
- PrivateLink provisioning: typically 3-5 business days after we receive AWS account IDs, target region, and subnet choices (depends on approvals on your end).
- VPC peering: can be faster technically (1-3 business days) but often blocked by CIDR overlap reviews and route management; requires both sides to make route table updates.
- Egress IPs / allowlisting: we offer two modes:
	• Redwood-hosted NAT: we can publish a small set (3-5) of static egress IPs for allowlisting. This is the easiest for customers who cannot NAT internally.
	• Customer-managed NAT: you NAT through your own gateway and allow our service IP ranges in the peering/route config.

I attached a diagram in the guide, but Raj - when you have a minute we can produce a tailored diagram showing your VPC CIDRs and the recommended setup. If you prefer PrivateLink, we only need the account ID and subnets for the interface endpoints; we will provide the service name and endpoint IDs.

Action items:
- Atlas: confirm preferred option + provide AWS account ID(s) & VPC CIDR(s) - Raj / NetOps to own (Alex to introduce contact).
- Redwood: schedule deep-dive with Dev (infra) + Sean (delivery) - I can send a calendar invite once we agree on a slot.
- Redwood: include a short note about Dedicated capacity tradeoffs (no private networking required but different isolation model + cost).

Proposed slots again: Mon 2/22 10-11 PT or Tue 2/23 1-2 PT. If those don't work, please share Raj's calendar link.

Thanks,
--Marissa
